memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: That is why a man leaves his father and mother and is united to his wife, and they become one flesh. — Gen 2:24 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Right here, at the very beginning of the Bible, God lays down the pattern for marriage. And it is worth remembering that this is God's idea, not merely a human custom that developed over time. Marriage was designed by the Lord Himself, and that gives it a dignity and beauty the world often forgets.

Three things stand out. First, a man leaves—a new family unit is formed, with its own priority and loyalty. Second, he is united to his wife—the word pictures a deep, committed bond, a holding fast that does not easily let go. Third, they become one flesh—a union of two whole lives into a shared oneness, body, heart, and purpose. This is far more than a contract; it is a covenant, a joining that God Himself makes.

Jesus quoted this very verse and added, "what God has joined together, let no one separate" (Matt 19:6). He treated marriage as sacred and lasting, a reflection of God's faithful, committed love.

Whether you are married or not, this design speaks to us all, for marriage is a living picture of something greater. Paul tells us it points to Christ and His church—the Bridegroom who leaves His Father's side, unites Himself to His people, and makes them one with Him forever (Eph 5:31–32). Every faithful marriage whispers of that greater, unbreakable love.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Do you view marriage as God's sacred design, or merely a human arrangement?
- If married, how can you nurture faithful, committed "one flesh" unity?
- How does Christ's covenant love for His church shape the way you love others?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord God, thank You for designing marriage as a picture of covenant love. Help those who are married to hold fast faithfully, and help us all to treasure the greater love of Christ for His people. Amen.
